transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Out on the trails and even back in town, I keep hearing and sensing things from the landscape telling me what to do with my work, and it’s starting to scare me. It feels like the mountains around Bozeman are speaking directly to me about my choreography, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
When you hear the mountains speaking to you, do you hear a clear, physical voice out loud as if someone is standing next to you, or is it more of a strong feeling or thought inside your mind?

It is definitely a clear, low voice that sounds like it's coming from the ridgelines or the buildings, not just a thought in my head. It tells me very specific things, like which dancers to fire or what colors to paint the studio walls. It feels so incredibly real that I've actually started avoiding certain trails and streets because I'm scared of what it will say next.
How long have you been hearing these voices and experiencing these feelings from the landscape?

They started earlier this year when I first signed the studio lease, lasting for about two months during a really revved-up, high-energy period. But once I crashed into this heavy depression—which has been going on for about nine months now—the voices and those feelings stopped completely.
Have you ever heard these voices or had these sensations during times when your mood felt completely stable and normal, rather than high-energy or depressed?

No, not at all. Those voices and sensations only happened during that wild, high-energy stretch when I was barely sleeping and buzzing with ideas. Once I crashed into this low, heavy phase, they stopped completely, and they've never shown up when my mood felt normal or stable.
During this heavy depression over the last nine months, how much has it impacted your ability to run your dance studio and manage your daily responsibilities?

It has completely devastated everything, and my studio is currently hanging by a thread. I’ve lost students, missed critical grant deadlines, and my business partner is threatening to pull out because I’m too withdrawn to run classes or answer emails. I can barely even manage basic chores at home right now; I just feel utterly overwhelmed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for Bipolar Affective Disorder, currently in a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms (F31.4). She describes a current 9-month episode of severe depression causing profound functional impairment in her professional and daily life, with no active psychotic symptoms. She also describes a past 2-month episode of mania characterized by high energy, decreased need for sleep, rapid ideas, and grandiose/somatic auditory hallucinations (hearing the mountains speak to her). Since the psychotic symptoms were confined to the past manic episode and are completely absent during the current severe depressive episode, F31.4 is the most accurate diagnosis.
